The '''2026 United States Senate election in South Carolina''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent [[South Carolina]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] appointee [[Darline Graham]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] pediatrician [[Annie Andrews (pediatrician)|Annie Andrews]] are the nominees for their respective parties.

Graham's brother, four-term incumbent [[Lindsey Graham|Lindsey]], won the Republican nomination in the June 9 primaries, but died on July 11. Appointed to her brother's seat and encouraged to run with the support of President [[Donald Trump]], Graham defeated congressman [[Ralph Norman]] in a runoff on August 25 with 52.5% of the vote after no candidate received a majority in an August 11 special primary. Andrews won the Democratic nomination with 61.5% of the vote over former [[Paine College]] administrator Brandon Brown.

The winner is expected<!--Do not change. Stating definitively in [[Wikipedia:Wikivoice|Wikivoice]] that the winner will be female is inappropriate. --> to be the first woman elected to the Senate from South Carolina. Democrats have not won a Senate election in the state since [[1998 United States Senate election in South Carolina|1998]].

== Background ==
South Carolina is generally considered a [[Red states and blue states|Republican stronghold]], having last elected a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] to the U.S. Senate in [[1998 United States Senate election in South Carolina|1998]]. Republican nominee [[Donald Trump]] won South Carolina in the [[2020 United States presidential election in South Carolina|2020 presidential election]] by 12 percentage points; in [[2024 United States presidential election in South Carolina|2024]], his margin grew to 18 points. Republicans control every statewide office (except the [[South Carolina Comptroller General|state's comptroller office]]) and have supermajorities in both chambers of the [[South Carolina State Legislature|state legislature]], both [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] seats, and all but one seat in South Carolina's [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] [[South Carolina's congressional delegations|congressional delegation]].<ref>{{Cite web |first1=Abraham |last1=Kenmore |first2=Seanna |last2=Adcox |date=November 6, 2024 |title=Trump wins SC for 3rd time, on his way to stunning White House victory |url=https://scdailygazette.com/2024/11/05/trump-wins-sc-for-3rd-consecutive-presidential-contest/ |access-date=December 21, 2024 |website=South Carolina Daily Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |first1=Jessica |last1=Holdman |first2=Abraham |last2=Kenmore |date=November 6, 2024 |title=SC Republicans celebrate red wave that gives GOP biggest advantage in 150 years |url=https://scdailygazette.com/2024/11/06/sc-republicans-celebrates-red-wave-that-gives-gop-strongest/ |access-date=December 7, 2024 |website=South Carolina Daily Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref>

Lindsey Graham was first elected in [[2002 United States Senate election in South Carolina|2002]], defeating Democrat [[Alex Sanders (politician)|Alex Sanders]] by about 10 percentage points. He was reelected in [[2008 United States Senate election in South Carolina|2008]], [[2014 United States Senate election in South Carolina|2014]], and most recently in [[2020 United States Senate election in South Carolina|2020]], defeating [[Jaime Harrison]] by 10 percentage points in what was expected to be a [[dead heat]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Lobosco |first1=Katie |date=November 4, 2020 |title=Lindsey Graham defeats Jaime Harrison in South Carolina |url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/11/03/politics/south-carolina-senate-race-2020/index.html |access-date=December 21, 2024 |publisher=CNN |language=en}}</ref> In January 2025, he declared that he was running for reelection.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Connaughton |first1=Kevin |date=January 14, 2025 |title=Lindsey Graham announces campaign team, funding for 2026 re-election bid |url=https://www.wistv.com/2025/01/14/lindsey-graham-announces-campaign-team-funding-2026-re-election-bid/ |access-date=June 17, 2025 |publisher=WIS-TV |language=en}}</ref> Graham died suddenly on July 11, 2026, of [[cardiac arrest]].<ref name="Cardiac">{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/sen-lindsey-graham-dies-71-brief-sudden-illness-rcna552722 |title=Sen. Lindsey Graham dies at 71 after 'brief and sudden illness' |website=NBC News |last1=Wong |first1=Scott |last2=Thorp V |first2=Frank |date=July 12, 2026 |access-date=July 12, 2026}}</ref>

==Special Republican primary==
Lindsey Graham, who had won the Republican primary, died on July 11, 2026. Under South Carolina law, a special primary election was held on August 11 to select a replacement Republican nominee.<ref name="Justia">{{cite web |title=2025 South Carolina Code of Laws Title 7 - Elections Chapter 11 - Designation And Nomination Of Candidates Section 7-11-55. Substitution of candidates when nominee selected by primary election |url=https://law.justia.com/codes/south-carolina/title-7/chapter-11/section-7-11-55/|website=Justicia|access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title= Title 7 - Elections CHAPTER 11 Designation and Nomination of Candidates ARTICLE 1 Methods of Nomination |url= https://www.scstatehouse.gov/Archives/CodeofLaws2023/t07c011.php |website= South Carolina Code of Laws |access-date= July 12, 2026}}</ref>

The three-week campaign was an unusually compressed U.S. Senate race.<ref>{{Cite web |date= July 13, 2026 |title= Graham Senate Seat Special Election: The Aug. 11 Primary – Democrats organized to vote with light turnout projected |url= https://myrtlebeachsc.com/graham-senate-seat-special-election/ |access-date= July 28, 2026 |work= Myrtle Beach SC News}}</ref> The candidate filing period opened at noon on July 21 and closed at noon on July 28.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Bain |first1= Sydni |date= July 13, 2026 |title= U.S. Senate Special Republican Party Filing & Primary |url= https://scvotes.gov/u-s-senate-special-republican-party-filing-primary/ |access-date= July 27, 2026 |website= SC Votes - South Carolina Election Commission |language= en-US}}</ref> The South Carolina State Election Commission ruled that the special Republican primary will be treated as a continuation of the June 9 primary. Accordingly, only voters who participated in the Republican primary or did not vote in either party's June 9 primary were eligible to vote; those who voted in the Democratic primary were ineligible, despite South Carolina's open primary system, which does not require party registration.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Moore |first1= Stephanie |date= July 13, 2026 |title= South Carolina to hold special primary for Lindsey Graham's Senate seat |url= https://www.wyff4.com/article/south-carolina-special-primary-lindsey-graham-seat/71917010 |website= WYFF}}</ref> Federal law generally requires military and overseas ballots to be mailed at least 45 days before a federal election, while the special election took take place 31 days after Lindsey Graham's death triggered the vacancy.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Wooten |first1= Alan |date= July 13, 2026 |title= Voters will choose Graham's successor on ballot through primary |url= https://www.thecentersquare.com/south_carolina/article_7446d7ac-09ea-437d-8fc5-efc7ba6e2ac6.html |website= The Center Square}}</ref> 

In June, the South Carolina Republican Party adopted a measure stating that to qualify for elected office in a Republican primary, a candidate must have voted in at least two of the last three statewide Republican primary elections.<ref>{{cite web |title= The Rules of the South Carolina Republican Party |url= https://sc.gop/wp-content/uploads/sites/14/2026/07/SCGOPRules2026.pdf |website= SC GOP |access-date= July 30, 2026}}</ref> On July 28, the South Carolina Republican Party decertified three candidates seeking the nomination. Clark Neilson was disqualified for not living in the state and Darius Mitchell and Danny Ford II were disqualified for not meeting the new state party requirement.<ref name= "Disqualified" /> On July 30, Ford announced that he was suing the South Carolina Republican party to be placed on the ballot. His attorney, state senator [[Brad Hutto]], said the party's new rule violates both the South Carolina and the US constitutions.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Reynolds |first1= Nick |date= July 30, 2026 |title= Danny Ford II, disqualified from the Republican US Senate race, sues SCGOP for ballot access |url= https://www.postandcourier.com/politics/danny-ford-scgop-senate-republican/article_243f2d3a-384f-4414-aadc-e830e41946ec.html |access-date= July 30, 2026 |website= [[The Post and Courier]]}}</ref> On August 3, [[Richland County, South Carolina|Richland County]] judge Daniel Coble ordered that Ford's name be on the ballot.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Biddix |first1= Stephen| last2= Kesler |first2= Alex| last3= Hemphill |first3= Joshua |date= August 4, 2026 |title= Judge rules Danny Ford II must appear on SC Senate primary ballot ahead of early voting |url= https://www.wistv.com/2026/08/04/judge-rules-danny-ford-ii-must-appear-senate-primary-ballot/ |access-date= August 5, 2026 |website= [[WIS (TV)]] |language= en}}</ref>

U.S. President [[Donald Trump]] said that if she ran in the primary he would endorse [[Darline Graham]], Lindsey Graham's sister.<ref name="politicojune17">{{cite web| url= https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/17/trump-endorses-darline-graham-for-lindsay-grahams-open-senate-seat-01003457| title= Trump endorses Darline Graham for Lindsey Graham's open Senate seat| last1= Johansen|first1= Ben| website= [[Politico]]| date= June 17, 2026}}</ref> By July 20, she announced she would run in the special primary for a full term. [[Ralph Norman]], [[Russell Fry]], [[Mark Sanford]], and Mark Lynch also launched campaigns.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://apnews.com/article/south-carolina-special-primary-senate-lindsey-graham-666830ac225c8dbf1027d041d9e88b31| title= AP Decision Notes: What to expect in South Carolina's special primary to replace Sen. Lindsey Graham| date= August 10, 2026| website= [[Associated Press]]| last1= Yoon|first1=Robert}}</ref> No candidate received a majority of the vote, so a runoff election between [[Darline Graham]] and [[Ralph Norman]] was held on August 25.<ref>{{Cite web |date= August 25, 2026 |title= Sen. Darline Graham wins the Republican Senate primary runoff in South Carolina |url= https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/darline-graham-winner-south-carolina-gop-senate-primary-rcna593581 |access-date= August 25, 2026 |website= NBC News| last1= Wong| first1= Scott}}</ref>

===Runoff===
Graham and Norman were considered closely matched in the primary, with Graham's endorsement by Trump weighing against Norman's legislative experience and reputation as a staunchly conservative outsider.<ref name= "PBS">{{cite web| url= https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/darline-graham-ralph-norman-go-head-to-head-in-south-carolinas-gop-senate-runoff |title= Darline Graham, Ralph Norman go head-to-head in South Carolina's GOP Senate runoff |website= PBS |last1= Kinnard |first1= Meg |agency= Associated Press |date= August 25, 2026 |access-date= August 27, 2026}}</ref> Trump vigorously campaigned for Graham, headlining a rally for her in [[Myrtle Beach]].<ref name= "DarlineWins">{{cite web| url= https://www.politico.com/news/2026/08/25/darline-graham-wins-south-carolina-senate-runoff-01050320 |title= Political newcomer Darline Graham wins South Carolina's GOP Senate runoff |website= Politico |last1= Hernandez |first1= Alec |date= August 25, 2026 |access-date= August 27, 2026}}</ref> He also made numerous calls to prominent South Carolina officials to secure their support for Graham, including to Russell Fry, who endorsed her on August 14, and to Governor McMaster, who held a press conference emphasizing his support for her.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/14/us/politics/russell-fry-darline-graham-south-carolina.html| title= Trump Pressured Russell Fry to Endorse Darline Graham for Senate. So He Did.| date= August 14, 2026| last1= Davies|first1= Emily| website= [[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date= August 24, 2026 |title= Gov. McMaster doubles down on endorsement of Darline Graham ahead of SC Senate runoff |url= https://www.wistv.com/2026/08/24/live-gov-mcmaster-sen-darline-graham-holding-press-conference/ |access-date= August 24, 2026 |website= WIS-TV |language= en}}</ref>

In ''[[The New York Times]]'', Michael Gold wrote that Trump had two main disputes with Norman that solidified his support for Graham: Norman's endorsement of [[Nikki Haley]] for president in [[Nikki Haley 2024 presidential campaign|2024]] and his votes (with other members of the [[House Freedom Caucus]]) against several pieces of legislation Trump supported on the grounds that they contained wasteful government spending. Most notably, Norman had initially refused to vote for Trump's flagship second-term policy, the [[One Big Beautiful Bill Act]], which Graham used as evidence that Norman was insufficiently committed to advancing Trump's agenda.<ref name="Gold">{{cite web| url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/24/us/politics/ralph-norman-trump-south-carolina.html |title= With Trump Against Him, Can Ralph Norman Win in South Carolina? |newspaper= The New York Times |last1= Gold |first1= Michael |date= August 24, 2026 |access-date= August 27, 2026}}</ref> Norman campaigned around the state, arguing that he had acted against Trump's wishes only because Trump was insufficiently conservative on government spending.<ref name= "Gold"/><ref>{{cite web |last1= Guzman |first1= Jenna |date= August 24, 2026 |title= Ralph Norman speaks to Horry County voters ahead of runoff election |url= https://www.wmbfnews.com/2026/08/24/ralph-norman-speaks-horry-county-voters-ahead-runoff-election/ |access-date= August 24, 2026 |website= WMBF-TV |language= en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title= Ralph Norman Holds Voter Town Hall in Anderson, SC Ahead of Aug. 25 Primary Runoff |url= https://www.c-span.org/program/campaign-2026/ralph-norman-holds-voter-town-hall-in-anderson-sc-ahead-of-aug-25-primary-runoff/684304 |access-date= August 24, 2026 |website= C-SPAN|language= en-us}}</ref>

== General election ==
[[Cost of living]], the [[economy]], [[War|foreign wars]], and the candidates' experience are the central issues for voters.<ref name= "Mazzei1">{{Cite news |last= Mazzei |first= Patricia |last2= Igielnik |first2= Ruth |date= October 28, 2026 |title= The Senate Race in Heavily Republican South Carolina is a Tossup, Poll Finds |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/28/us/south-carolina-florida-minnesota-poll.html |access-date= October 29, 2026 |work= The New York Times |language= en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

The seat was initially considered safe for Republicans, but after Graham said during a debate that she was "not that informed on [[national security]]" and some voters began to see her as inexperienced and unqualified to be a senator, the race became a contested tossup.<ref name= "Mazzei1" /> A ''[[The New York Times]]/[[Siena University (New York)|Siena]]'' poll found that "51 percent of the voters in the polls, including 18 percent of Republicans" said Graham "did not have the right experience to be an effective senator". In contrast, "54 percent of voters, including 22 percent of Republicans, said that Dr. Andrews did."<ref name="Mazzei1" />
